en: Oh, did you now?
Yeah! All that chasing you did managed to wear the ol' girl down. By the time I caught up, she looked like she was ready to drop!
That's good to hear. I'm glad my running amounted to more than just exercise.
Oh, no, you were a big help, really. It wasn't easy, was it? The way she can scuttle around like a chicken with her head⑬well, still on.
Yeah, that bird was freakishly fast.
Hahaha, but of course. This beaut right here ain't your garden variety gamecock. She's a certified, bona fide Cochin!
Yeah? Cochin's that expensive breed used for premium-grade meat, right? Mmm, I've never had any before.
No way! You're not eating this little prizehen. Don't look at my Cochin with those lustful, greedy eyes!
Oh, and I hear the eggs are as tasty as the meat. An oyakodon bowl made with Cochin must taste like heaven.
Purge those unclean thoughts from your mind! This bird is precious beyond compare! Why, eating her would be a cardinal sin!
I dunno, man, seems like a waste of good bird to me. What's so special about this one?
I'll show you. I promised you a reward for helping, right? Come with me.
Oh, and the name's Ukai. What's yours?
Shinada. I'm a freelance journalist specializing in... how should I put this? Ever want to hit up a massage parlor? I'm the guy to ask.
Oh, huh, how interesting. Nice to meet you, Shinada-san.
So? Where are we off to?
You'll see when we get there. It's right over yonder.
Behold! For you are about to witness the greatest competition of luck, pluck, and cluck ever devised! <Italic>This</Italic> is the Cochin Cup Classic!
Cochin Cup Classic? Never heard of it.

Think of this like a sanctuary for chicken enthusiasts.
A place where people take the beloved Cochins they've
nurtured and race them against each other for prize money.
It's not unlike horse racing, really. There are some champion birds out there that've hauled in millions.
Millions? As in millions of yen? Seriously!?
Honest truth, buddy. That bird we just bagged? Her eggs are as good as gold.
Huh. Sounds like there's good money to be made. So did you come up with this Cochin racing idea on your own?
Yep. Not to crow about it, but it sure is something, ain't it?

I used to run a chicken farm out in the countryside, see.
One day, I set up a track on a whim and raced us some birds.
And wouldn't you know it⑬people got a big hoot out of it.
I figured what works in the sticks has a chance to soar in Kineicho, so I gave it a try. Pretty soon the spectacle became a full-on sport.
We've been getting betters and breeders in droves. The latter of which can sure make a mint! Thoroughbred race Cochins are their livelihood now.
Well how about that.
So. Shinada-san. I'll give you an up-and-coming Cochin in my stable as thanks for bringing my little chickadee home.
Really? You will?
You have to promise me you won't eat it, though. You're only getting it on the condition that you raise it as a proper racer.
If you do it right, that chicken can make you a lot more money than it can as meat.
Even millions, huh?
Absolutely. Talk to me if you want to enter it in a race. I'll set things up for you.
Let's step outside.
Huh, I had no idea there were races held here.
Yeah, well, this is where I spend most of my life. Ever get the urge to send a chicken flyin' down the track⑬you come talk to me.
Oh, and here you go, buddy. The Cochin I promised you.
You got an <Color:8>Intelligent-looking Cochin Chicken<Color:Default>.
(Cochin races, huh? Maybe I'll give it a shot.)

You can enter your Cochin in a race by speaking to Ukai.
Winning a race will net you a cash prize.

The higher the race's rank, the better the prize.

There are four ranks in total:
Newcomer, Challenger, Contender, and Champion.

To win higher-ranked races, your Cochin will need training.
Aim for the top of the Champion Class!
Will you be participating in the Cochin Cup Classic? Oh hey, if it isn't Shinada-san, my chicken-chasing comrade!
Hm? You still haven't named the Cochin I gave you?
Oh... right. It is a living creature. I guess it does need a name.
Yeah, he'll need a proper name in order to register for the races. Why don't we go ahead and take care of that right now?
Okay, I'll take this baby in. Tell me whenever you want to race it.
Oh, hey, you have a new Cochin to race? I'll take it in, then.
I'll take care of the race registration. What's his name?
Hey, it looks like you've got a new Cochin to race. I'll take it in, then.
Shinada-san, your Cochin qualified for the Champion Class. Good work! And good luck!
Shinada, your Cochin's made it to the Contender Class. The competition's going to ramp up, so do your best!
Shinada-san, your Cochin qualified for the Challenger Class. This is where the racing really starts. Good luck!

Howdy. Here's where you can enter the Cochin Cup Classic.
Now what can I do for you, fella?
Enter a Cochin in a race.
You can hire a trainer to raise your Cochin. You'll need to pay them, though.
You can mate your roosters with a hen and breed a brand-new bird.
I can make your Cochin forget an unwanted skill. No, seriously.
You can check the growth parameters of any Cochin I'm holding for you.
You can view the titles a Cochin has earned. You can switch titles here, too.
What, you want to know about the Cochin Cup Classic?
Aww, you're leaving?
The Cochins are all exhausted. They can't race anymore.
You can't enter any more races like this. At this rate, you should breed a new Cochin and raise it for racing.
Which class are you going to enter?
The starting class for any Cochin. Train it up and aim for the higher classes.
This is one rank up from Newcomer. You'll be competing against better-trained Cochins.
You'll see some stiff competition here, one step away from the Champion Class.
This is the most challenging class. Only the fastest and the toughest are allowed to race.
The Wind Cup. It's a short course that has no special features.
The Novice Cup. It's a short course that has some dirt on it.
The Chicken Cup. It's a short course that has a dirt stretch at the start.
The Drake Cup. It's a short course that has a long dirt stretch from the middle onwards.
The Dawn Cup. The hardest of the Newcomer Class, it's a short course with dirt in the second half.
Oh, you're not going to race.
The winner earns 1,000 yen. Want to enter this race?
Off you go, then. Good luck!
The winner earns 1,500 yen. Want to enter this race?
The Kamikaze Cup. It's a long course with no especially notable features.
The Rising Cup. It's a long course with patches of dirt here and there.
The Silver Cup. It's a long course with a middle section that's almost all dirt. You need a Cochin with high dirt performance here.
The Crystal Cup. It's a long course with dark sections. It won't be a big factor in this race, but know that Cochins do slow down in darkness.
The Shigure Cup. The toughest of the Challenger Class, it's a long course with frequent dark stretches.
The winner earns 2,000 yen. Want to enter this race?
The winner earns 2,500 yen. Want to enter this race?
The Tortoise Cup. It's a short course where Contender Class speedsters can tear it up.
The Phoenix Cup. It's a short course with extended dirt patches early.
The Tiger Cup. It's a short course with frequent dark spots. The short distance makes it tough to make up ground.
The Dragon Cup. It's a long, oddball course with almost all of it in dirt or darkness. An average Cochin stands no chance.
The Adamant Cup. The toughest of the Contender Class, it's a long, athletic course with dirt in the first half and darkness in the second half.
The winner earns 3,000 yen. Want to enter this race?
The winner earns 3,500 yen. Want to enter this race?
The King Cup. A short course with no obstacles. It's all about Leg Power here. This is the introduction to the Champion Class.
The Storm Cup. A short course that's almost entirely composed of dirt. Beside Leg Power, it's a test of dirt performance.
The Black Cup. A long course with frequent dark stretches. Entrants are often specially trained to race well in the dark.
The Skanda Cup. A long course that's all dirt in the second half. Leg Power and Stamina are the order of the day for this challenging run.
The Azuchi Cup. The pinnacle of all courses, meant for the toughest and fastest. Win here to prove yourself a true Cochin master.
The winner earns 4,000 yen. Want to enter this race?
The winner earns 4,500 yen. Want to enter this race?
Hm? Ah, your Cochins have reached the limits of their growth potential.
There's no point in trying to tamper with these perfect manifestations of poultry. You should focus on breeding the next generation.
Which Cochin are you gonna train?
Which trainer are you gonna go with?
Shimazaki emphasizes Stamina in his training. He has a huge appetite, so he's happy when he gets food.
Toda concentrates on Leg Power. The man loves his liquor⑬I see him drunk off his ass all the time.
Yasaka has a thing against concentrating on any one parameter, so his training is evenly balanced. He likes his basic sundries.
Kanamiya's training is all about throwing money at improving Traction and Night Vision. He's a sure hand, but his tastes are expensive.
Shimazaki's your choice? What are you giving him as payment?
Toda-san it is. What are you gonna give him as payment?
You chose Yasaka. What are you giving him as payment?
Got it, Kanamiya's your man. What are you giving him as payment?
All right. Now you might have to be a little patient. You know how they say it's a virtue? Well they're right.
That should do it. Next time you want to have a trainer work on your Cochin, let me know.
Hmm. Your Cochins are still young and have plenty of growth potential.
Be mindful that poor breeding leads to poor results. Let your Cochins run and grow some more first.
When you breed, the chick can inherit only up to four skills from the parent. Don't forget.
Now there's a prodigy with a promising future! Try to raise it to its full potential.
Here, this is yours, too.
You got a <Color:8>Yakitori<Color:Default>.
You don't have a Cochin that needs to forget a skill. Looking good!
I can purge unwanted skills from a Cochin. Which one should I treat?
Okay. It will cost you 5,000 yen, though. Do you want to do it?
Oops, sorry, you don't have the money. Come back when your wallet isn't quite so light.
Okay, give me a little time.
Foul skill... Begone!
There, I'm done. Try to give it a more suitable skill.
Which Cochin do you want to check?
Which Cochin's titles do you want to check? You can switch their titles, too.
The Cochin Cup Handbook has useful information.

Welcome to the Cochin Cup Classic! Work your way through
the races as an owner to reach the top of the <Color:7>Champion Class<Color:Default>!
No new Cochin can win race after race on potential alone⑬
they must be trained to develop their abilities.

There is a limit to a Cochin's development, and
it can run only so many races until it is worn
out. If it reaches its natural limit, <Color:7>breed<Color:Default> its
next generation. While the chick's parameters
will start out lower than the parent's, it has
more potential to grow as it begins racing.

Repeat the cycle of racing, breeding, and training to
create elite bloodlines for victory in the Champion Class!
What do you want to know about parameters?

<Color:7>Leg Power<Color:Default> directly equates to speed⑬the higher
the better. Stamina indicates endurance.

The higher the Leg Power, the quicker <Color:7>Stamina<Color:Default> is
drained. If your bird's Leg Power rises, make
sure to train it to boost its Stamina as well.

<Color:7>Traction<Color:Default> indicates how well the bird runs in dirt. The higher the better.
<Color:7>Night Vision<Color:Default> indicates how resistant the bird is to slowing in darkness. The higher the value, the better it will run in the dark.

There are a wide variety of skills⑬some boost
your bird's parameters, while others make it
more likely to stop. Skills can be learned when
<Color:7>training or breeding<Color:Default>, but not always. A bird can
learn up to five skills.

There are five <Color:7>condition<Color:Default> levels, ranging from Perfect to Lousy. Condition changes over time,
or as a bird races. The better its condition, the more a bird's parameters will rise during a race.
